newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU assembly demands Zaire's Mobutu resign.
newsitem.headline: EU assembly demands Zaire's Mobutu resign.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday demanded the resignation of Zairean President Mobutu and his government, and the holding of democratic elections.

"(The European Parliament stresses) the need to find a peaceful political solution to the conflict in Zaire that will put an end to the regime of Mr Mobutu Sese Seko with a view to the introduction of a democratic system," the parliament said in a resolution.
The call came a day after Mobutu sacked Prime Minister Etienne Tshisekedi, appointed only last week, and replaced him with former Defence Minister General Likulia Bolongo.
In Brussels, Belgian Foreign Minister Erik Derycke said Zaire was now in the hands of a military dictatorship.

European Commissioner Manuel Marin told the European Union assembly the west must keep up pressure "for a cessation of hostilities and the setting up of a transitional government which will start the process of democratisation".

The EU parliament appealed for an immediate ceasefire between the Zairean army and rebels led by Laurent Kabila who have taken control of mineral- and diamond-rich eastern Zaire and are advancing on the capital Kinshasa.
European governments must give full backing to South African efforts to broker direct negotiations between the Mobutu regime and the rebels, the assembly said.
